rejected.done_when: The customer is verified and logged once, or has been told they could not be verified. Their referral history (the 9-day window and the per-type annual counts) and their account tenure have been checked from the records, and any of their own figures that differ from the records have been corrected. Then one of three outcomes holds. (a) The customer was told the referral cannot be submitted now and why: the rolling window is full, tenure is too short, they share a registered address, the referred party is not new or has the same business owner, the signer is under 18, or no program's deposit, cap or age rule is met. No recommendation was given and nothing was submitted. (b) The customer was told the eligible account to use, with both bonus amounts, the qualifying deposit and its window, and the conditions. The account was ranked by the goal they stated (combined or own bonus), or by the active business promotion's priority among programs that pass every check; or they were asked and chose from the passing accounts. They have run submit_referral with that account's name as its documents write it (or know to do so), and the result has been explained. (c) For several parties: each party has a recommended account or a reason it has none. A party whose every option is blocked (for example by annual caps, including caps used up by other parties in this conversation) was told why and was not submitted. The customer has submitted no more referrals than there are open slots, in the order they chose, after saying whether 'maximize the bonus' means their own or the combined bonus. For each party still waiting, they know the account to use and when a slot opens.
